title: Google launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal with Cleary, Freshfields, Weil, and Williams & Connolly
subtitle: The first vertical packaging of Gemini Enterprise ships legal-specific skills, connectors into iManage, NetDocuments, RelativityOne, and Harvey, and an agent path for brief drafting and DSAR fulfillment.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google Cloud launched Gemini Enterprise for Legal on August 25, a purpose-built configuration of its enterprise Gemini platform aimed at law firms and corporate legal departments. Cleary Gottlieb, Freshfields, Weil Gotshal & Manges, and Williams & Connolly are named launch firms. The product ships in preview with pre-built agents for brief drafting, citation verification, contract lifecycle management, regulatory horizon scanning, and data subject access request (DSAR) fulfillment, and it connects into iManage, NetDocuments, RelativityOne, Docusign, Everlaw, Legora, Harvey, and Thomson Reuters. A parallel financial services edition was announced the same day.

The interesting move is the shape of the go-to-market. Rather than building a horizontal enterprise product and letting firms plumb it in, Google is packaging Gemini into a vertical with the ISVs it needs to matter to legal work already integrated. That includes Harvey — the legal-AI startup that competes with Google's own agents — as a connector partner, not a competitor to be walled off. In big-law procurement, integration lists are half the sale; naming Harvey and iManage on day one accelerates the deployment path.

For Google DeepMind, the launch is also a distribution answer to a question that has been open all year: what does Google's frontier-model advantage look like in an enterprise market where OpenAI and Anthropic have gone first? The answer is starting to be legible: pick verticals where document volume, retrieval quality, and long-context reasoning matter, and ship a configuration with the workflow tools already wired in. Legal is a good test case because the firms that make it work will pay real money for it, and the ones that don't will lose associate leverage to the ones that do.

For learners: legal is one of the few AI markets where quality of citations matters more than fluency. When you evaluate a legal AI product — as a student, a paralegal, or a client — check how it handles citation verification. A model that drafts a clean brief but hallucinates a case number is dangerous; a model that refuses to draft a paragraph until it has verified the cite is useful. Correct behavior under uncertainty is the feature worth paying for.
